s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Creatinine level is 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level is 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: central retinal artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: sudden vision loss in one eye with relative afferent pupillary defect and retinal findings

shortlist.label: acute angle closure
shortlist.why_kept: elevated intraocular pressure and vision loss in one eye

shortlist.label: optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss and pain in one eye with relative afferent pupillary defect

shortlist.label: giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss and orbital inflammation in a patient over 30

shortlist.label: retinal detachment
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss and retinal findings on Optical Coherence Tomography

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden vision loss in one eye, no light perception in the right eye, and findings such as delayed retinal arterial filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography, along with severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography, are highly suggestive of central retinal artery occlusion.

rejected.label: acute angle closure
rejected.why: Intraocular pressure is elevated but not as high as typically seen in acute angle closure, and there's no mention of a mid-dilated pupil that reacts poorly to light, which is common in acute angle closure.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: Optic neuritis typically presents with pain on eye movement and a central visual field defect, which is not the primary complaint here, and the imaging findings do not support optic neuritis as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: There's no mention of symptoms such as jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, or polymyalgia rheumatica, which are often associated with giant cell arteritis, and the patient's age and presentation do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: retinal detachment
rejected.why: While serous retinal detachment is mentioned, it is not the primary finding, and the overall clinical picture including the acute onset of vision loss and specific angiography findings points more towards a vascular occlusive event rather than a primary retinal detachment.
